messages:
Sam: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to lock the SDK surface for cursor-based pagination + retry/backpressure guarantees before the transport refactor PR. Thoughts on the minimal invariants?
Priya: What invariants are you thinking? idempotency, resume semantics, or backpressure signals?
Sam: All three tbh. Specifically: 1) SDK iterators must be restartable from a stable resume token; 2) retries should only be automatic for idempotent pages; 3) SDK should expose backpressure hooks for streaming paging.
Josh: My 2cts: make the resume token opaque. Transport owns validation. SDK stores it and passes back to server for resume. That avoids per-client parsing bugs.
Emma: Agree on opaque token. Also: distinguish between "page-level" retries (retry fetching the same cursor) and "global" retries (retry whole iteration). We should default to page-level with exponential backoff.
Leah: For backpressure: SDK should surface a low-level callback so consumers can pause intake if their consumer queue is full. E.g. on_pause/on_resume handlers on the iterator. Keep defaults aggressive for PLG users.
Josh: Example pseudocode we discussed earlier:
```python
# python iterator shape
for page in client.items.list_pages(limit=100, resume_token=None):
    process(page.items)
    save_checkpoint(page.resume_token)
```
Where page.resume_token is opaque str and page.is_last bool.
Priya: Cross-language note: Python -> generator, TS -> AsyncIterable, Go -> channel/iterator pattern. We should document parity but accept idiomatic differences.
Sam: Retry mapping proposal: auto-retry on [429, 502, 503, 504]. Do not auto-retry on 400/401/403/404. For retryable 5xx, do per-page retry with jittered exponential backoff.
Emma: Also add a max_total_retry_time per iteration to avoid infinite loops when cursor keeps bumping server side. Suggest default 60s.
Leah: For durable resume, we should include a checkpointing helper in SDK that atomically persists resume token + last-seen item id. This avoids duplicates on resume.
Josh: On transport semantics: if server returns a changed schema for page tokens (new format), client should treat resume_token as opaque and let server handle compatibility. SDK can warn if token TTL is near expiry (if server returns ttl).
Priya: Edge case: partial page consumption then crash. We should provide a small helper 'ack' API: page.mark_consumed() so we can checkpoint post-ack. Otherwise users will have to dedupe.
Sam: I like mark_consumed. Make it optional; default flow: SDK returns page, caller calls save_checkpoint(manual) or SDK can auto-checkpoint after iterator yields. Document tradeoffs.
deploy-bot: RFC doc updated: https://r.redd.co/rfc/cursor-retries (edited) :white_check_mark:
Priya: One more: expose `retry_policy` object in client config so teams can tune backoff, max_retries, and total_retry_time per-call. Keep sane defaults.
Emma: Also capture metrics: page_latency, retry_count, resume_success_rate. Console dashboards will need these for Optimize suggestions.
Sam: Action items: I'll draft a concise SDK surface PR: - opaque resume_token + is_last + mark_consumed API - default retry map + per-page backoff + max_total_retry_time - cross-lang iterator patterns and helper for checkpointing. I'll link PR in this thread by EOD.
Josh: :thumbsup:
Leah: :+1:
Priya: Thanks — ping me if you want help writing the TS/Go examples.
Sam: Thanks all — will follow up with PR and a short compatibility test harness for transports.
